title: Existence of the normalized affine cohomology edge morphism
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, phi : B → A, i an integer, and assume the sheaf derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Put T_R = tilde and f = Spec(phi). Given any ordinary natural comparison isomorphism sigma : res_phi ⋙ T_B ≅ T_A ⋙ f_*, define q_(C,i) by the inverse exact-homology comparison, inverse Q/homology comparison, H^i(Q(sigma_C)), and H^i of the right-derived unit [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Define b_(C,t) as the tilde unit followed by Gamma_A of inverse exact-tilde homology comparison, inverse Q/homology comparison, and H^i(t) [def-pc-affine-base-change-tilde-coordinates]. There exists a natural transformation alpha : T_B res_phi Gamma_A H^i → H^i Rf_* on D_QCoh(Spec A) [lem-pc-affine-derived-cohomology-presentation]. For every unbounded complex C, every L in that category, and every t : Q(T_A C) ≅ L with t.hom = eqToHom of an object equality, q_(C,i) followed by H^i(Rf_*t) equals T_B res_phi(b_(C,t)) followed by alpha_L. No invertibility of alpha is asserted.

proof.text: Apply exists_affineDerivedPushforwardSheafEdge to obtain the sheaf-level edge epsilon, with its derived-unit normalization. Transfer finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation from scalar restriction followed by tilde_B across the supplied sigma, so tilde_A followed by pushforward preserves homology.

Construct alpha by whiskering sigma with Gamma_A H^i, followed by pushforward of the tilde/Gamma counit, then epsilon. These are composites of natural transformations. Eliminate the object equality in the normalization hypothesis and use Iso.ext to reduce t to the identity.

Naturality of sigma moves the representative coordinate map across sigma. Naturality of the counit and the left triangle identity cancel the tilde unit, leaving pushforward of the inverse exact-homology and Q/homology comparisons. Apply the sheaf-edge normalization. Finally homologyMap_mapNatTrans and naturality of homologyFunctorFactors identify the remaining composite with the specified q.

theorem exists_affinePushforwardCohomologyEdge
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : B →+* A) (i : ℤ)
    (σ : ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ ⋙ affinePushforwardTilde B ≅
      affinePushforwardTilde A ⋙
        Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) :
  ∃ α : affineDerivedCohomologyModules A i ⋙
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ ⋙ affinePushforwardTilde B) ⟶
    (schemeDerivedQCohProperty (Spec (.of A))).ι ⋙
      schemeDerivedDirectImage (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of B)).toRingedSpace)) i,
    ∀ (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
      (L : schemeDerivedQCohCategory (Spec (.of A)))
      (t : DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((affinePushforwardTilde A).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C) ≅ L.obj),
      (∃ h : DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((affinePushforwardTilde A).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C) = L.obj,
        t.hom = eqToHom h) →
      affinePushforwardCohomologyMapOfComparison A B φ σ C i ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of B)).toRingedSpace)) i).map
          ((schemeDerivedDirectImage (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))).map t.hom) =
        (affinePushforwardTilde B).map ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).map
          (affinePushforwardRepresentativeCohomologyIso A C L.obj t i).hom) ≫ α.app L
